Revolutionary Voices Podcast

Open the Script Builder

Your group makes a 2 to 4 minute podcast episode about a person or group from the Revolution whose story is often left out. You build the script on voices.mrbsocialstudies.org, record it in WeVideo, and the class listens to every episode on Monday, November 9.

Why does your person or group matter to the story of the Revolution?

Your answer is your thesis. Your whole episode backs it up, and your Wrap says it out loud.

Listen to Mr. B’s sample episode about Haym Salomon to hear what a finished one sounds like.

Jobs

Everyone has at least one job, and everyone speaks. Jobs can be shared or split. In a group of two, share them.

Researcher

Before writing: Leads the reading and fills in the Fact Bank. Every fact gets a source. Makes sure the group has a source we found.

While writing: Checks the facts in the Doc. Adds a comment when a line needs a source.

Lead Scriptwriter

Before writing: Picks a style for each part and fills in the plan.

While writing: Puts everyone’s lines in order in the Doc.

Chief Editor

Before writing: Watches the time and this sheet.

While writing: Edits in Suggesting mode, so changes show up as suggestions. Makes sure everyone has lines, and times a read-aloud.

Parts You Can Say

  • Host: Talks to listeners and asks the questions.
  • Narrator: Sets the scene and moves the story along.
  • Subject: The person from history, speaking as “I.”

Six topics are about people who were enslaved. In those episodes nobody plays the person: the Narrator tells their story and reads real words from the time, saying who said them.

What You Bring

  • Each of you: Two or more facts from your Research Notes, each with where it came from. You type them into My Lines.
  • Your group: At least one source you found yourselves, in a library database or online, besides your reading. The Researcher can use a source a groupmate found, or put several together.

Your source line, said by the Host in the Wrap: “We learned about [person] from ___ and ___.”

How Your Episode Is Graded

Building a product that makes a claim

SSS4.6-8.1

Proficient (3): Every part of your work supports the same clear claim.

In your episode: Your Hook, Story and Wrap all back up your thesis, and the Wrap says it.

Crediting sources correctly

SSS4.6-8.2

Proficient (3): You cite your sources in the right format, both in your work and on your reference page.

In your episode: The Host says the source line, and your Group Doc ends with a list of your sources.

Analyzing what different groups contributed

H2.6-8.6

Proficient (3): You explain and analyze how a cultural or ethnic group shaped U.S. history.

In your episode: Your episode explains what your person or group did and how it changed the Revolution.

Every episode must:

  • Everyone speaks.
  • The episode runs 2 to 4 minutes.
  • Every fact comes from your notes or a source you can name.
  • You read clearly, so listeners understand every line.

Ready to Record

Check every one before you record on Thursday.

  • The whole script is in the Group Doc, and every line starts with who says it.
  • Each of us marked our lines: a slash ( / ) where we pause, and a line under the words we stress.
  • We read it all the way through twice, and Practice timed it at 2 to 4 minutes.
  • Mr. B heard us read 30 seconds.

The script builder saves your work on the Chromebook you use, so use the same one every day. The Group Doc is the copy your whole group shares.
